title: Scaling Laws of Ensemble Uncertainty in Language Models
abstract: arXiv:2611.32801v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Many use cases for large language models (LLMs)---from AI safety to exploration and human interaction---can benefit from epistemic uncertainty estimates. We argue that existing Bayesian Deep Learning solutions, which are often restricted to a fixed model family, fail to capture the full epistemic uncertainty at practical LLM scales. This is because the error due to the bounded capacity of the model family remains invisible to disagreement among models supported by the prior. We relate this error to the well-known power-law scaling of LLM loss with model size. We then show that a second power law quantifies the shrinking disagreement within ensembles as model size increases. Its slower decay relative to the capacity law above suggests that ensembles capture a growing share of epistemic uncertainty and become more competitive as an axis for scaling, compared to a single larger model. translated_title: 语言模型中集成不确定性的缩放定律
translated_abstract: 大型语言模型（LLM）的许多应用场景——从AI安全到探索与人类交互——都能从认知不确定性估计中受益。我们认为，现有的贝叶斯深度学习解决方案通常局限于固定的模型族，在实际的LLM规模下无法捕捉完整的认知不确定性。这是因为由模型族有限容量导致的误差，对于先验所支持的模型之间的分歧而言是不可见的。我们将这一误差与著名的LLM损失随模型规模的幂律缩放联系起来。随后，我们证明第二条幂律量化了集成内部分歧随模型规模增大而缩小的现象。相对于上述容量定律，该幂律较慢的衰减速度表明，集成能够捕获越来越多的认知不确定性份额，与单个更大的模型相比，集成作为一条扩展路径变得更具竞争力。最后，第三条幂律量化了集成……（摘要在此处截断）
tldr: 本文提出三条幂律缩放定律，证明集成随模型规模增大会捕获越来越多的认知不确定性，作为扩展路径相比单个更大的模型更具竞争力。
en_tdlr: This paper establishes three power-law scaling laws showing that ensembles capture a growing share of epistemic uncertainty as model size increases, making ensembles an increasingly competitive scaling axis compared to a single larger model.
